categories.name: Supported pairing declined for lack of shortlist variety
categories.definition: The run has evidence for a specific pairing or recommendation but declines because it cannot produce multiple distinct candidates, or treats the available detail as too limited, instead of testing distinct, grounded readings of the evidence already retrieved.

categories.name: Unrequested source search
categories.definition: The run searches a source that was not requested and is not necessary to answer the request, violating the expected routing or source boundary.

categories.name: Near-match memory returned as recall
categories.definition: The run treats a record with only a broad or adjacent subject overlap as a match to a specific personal-memory question.

categories.name: Decline reason misstates remaining evidence
categories.definition: The run chooses a decline reason that does not describe the actual limitation remaining after unusable evidence is excluded.

target_category: Supported pairing declined for lack of shortlist variety
diagnosis: The target failures repeatedly treat a single clear pairing as insufficient because the proposal contract requires two or three eligible candidates. The existing rule says candidates may read the same records differently, but does not explain how to distinguish a genuinely different interpretation from a restatement or how a narrower reading can be a valid runner-up. This differs from the correction kept in the earlier round: that correction clarified when concise public descriptions may support bounded claims; this edit addresses the separate problem of generating and ranking a second interpretation while retaining the eligibility threshold and decline option.

edits.find:
Distinct means different
interpretations, not different passages: two candidates may read the same pair
of records differently, as long as the shortlist as a whole cites at least two
records.
edits.replace: When one specific pairing is well supported, do not assume it permits only one reading or that the shortlist needs two independent bridges. Test whether the same evidence supports meaningfully different emphases—for example, how the passages develop or contrast each other, or what remains unresolved. A narrower reading can be a valid runner-up if it adds a distinct, evidence-grounded angle; rank it below the stronger reading when appropriate. Do not merely restate a candidate, invent missing details, or elevate a shared subject into a structure. Distinct means different interpretations, not different passages: two candidates may read the same pair of records differently, as long as the shortlist as a whole cites at least two records.
edits.reason: Give concrete guidance for developing a distinct runner-up from a supported pairing, while forbidding restatements, invented details, and topic-only links.

risks: The added guidance could encourage a second reading when only one is supportable, especially for a vague cue or passages that share only a topic. It explicitly rejects mere restatement, invented details, and topic-only links; both readings must still meet every eligibility anchor, and it directs a decline if no second interpretation is supported without forcing the evidence. A one-passage case also remains unable to meet the existing requirement that the shortlist cite at least two records. These constraints should preserve the passing declines while helping distinguish a valid narrower reading from an unsupported one.
